title: Every session verification and every sessionInventory operation produces one structured audit event on an allow-list of fields
description: The session verifier emits exactly one structured audit event per verification attempt (success or refusal) and per `sessionInventory` operation. Each event carries fields drawn from a fixed allow-list: `outcome`, `operation`, `reasonClass`, `sessionIdPrefix`, `at`, `principalIdPrefix?`. No event may carry the `__session` cookie value, the full session id, a raw Clerk claim, or a substring of any of the above. The `sessionIdPrefix` field is a substring of length no greater than eight characters. Every event is written to the audit sink synchronously with the verification result; a sink failure logs a `clerk.audit_sink_failed` warning event and never causes the verification to succeed spuriously. The blueprint's data-retention boundary is: audit events survive process restart when the sink is durable, and are treated as retained per the project's wider observability policy; the blueprint does not itself expire them.
rationale: The audit-surface responsibilities on TAC-1003 (verification events and sessionInventory events) are only observable if a REQ names the allow-list, the prefix boundary, and the sink-failure posture. Without a REQ, a reviewer cannot decide whether an event that carries an unexpected field violates the blueprint's contract.
